title: Bring energy from waste into carbon trading on time
noun: bringing energy from waste into carbon trading on time
headline: Carbon-price waste burning on time. Raises £0.5bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget delays bringing waste incinerators into the UK Emissions Trading Scheme, which costs £0.5 billion a year in lost permit revenue from 2029-30. Switch this on to bring them in on time.

baselinePolicy.text: Energy from waste joins the UK Emissions Trading Scheme later than planned; the delay costs from 2028-29 (Table 6.1 line 96).

source.quote: This measure delays the expansion of the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) to include greenhouse gas emissions generated from Energy from Waste (EfW) and waste incineration.

alreadyIncludes: Energy from waste joins the UK Emissions Trading Scheme later than planned; the delay costs from 2028-29 (Table 6.1 line 96).

lines.title: Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS): Delay the inclusion of energy from waste in the ETS

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
